title: Leo Package Registry
description: Catalog of installable data-driven (no-rebuild) Leo packages.

name.description: Unique id. Used as a settings-key component, plugin URL segment, and MCP package name.

provides.description: Subsystems this package's MCP server stands in for. Tools are what a package gives Claude; a provider is what it gives Leo — the wallpaper generator, the web_search tool and the speech pipeline each call one. The linked server must answer that role's tool: wallpaper -> search_photos, web_search -> search, tts -> synthesize (voices optional). Filling a role is shown at consent and is part of the install digest, so a role cannot be added after approval without the digest moving.

entitlements.description: Capabilities the package needs, consented to at install. The broker grants exactly these — least privilege.

feed.description: May post to the user's feed.

settings_read.description: Settings keys (e.g. API keys) the package may read — and only these.

network.description: Hostnames the package's process may reach.

sends.description: What classes of the owner's data leave the box, to which destination, and why — one entry per host. `network` says WHERE a package may dial; this says WHAT goes there, which is the half an owner actually needs to consent. A host in `network` with no entry here is reported at install as 'does NOT say what data it sends to …'.

dataflow.description: One destination and what the package admits to sending it. A declaration naming no class, or no purpose, is a defect and is refused at install rather than shown as a disclosure.

classes.description: Coarse data classes (search_queries, prompts, conversations, mail, financial, …). Deliberately coarse: this is read at a consent prompt, not queried.

because.description: Why, in the owner's terms — shown verbatim at consent.

appspec.description: App package: a standalone binary built from git on the host and run as a subprocess (NOT linked into Leo).

rev.description: Pinned commit SHA. The hub fetches this exact commit and verifies the checkout against it, so the reviewed code is the built code.

branch.description: Fallback when `rev` is absent — a mutable reference the author can move after review. Deprecated for new entries.

build.description: Build command run in the clone (default: cargo build --release).

bin.description: Path to the built binary, relative to the clone root.

port.description: Fixed port, or 0 to assign a free one at spawn.

bundle.description: Frontend bundle. sha256 is REQUIRED for the public registry so a compromised host cannot inject JavaScript.
